output.name: Viewer cache not invalidated on ECO release
output.summary: After an ECO releases a new drawing revision, plant users still see the old revision in the viewer until support manually clears the server-side viewer cache.

root_cause.text: Likely the ECO release event does not trigger invalidation or refresh of the server-side viewer cache, so the cache keeps serving the superseded revision.

quotes.quote: ECO released this morning but the viewer still shows revision B of 330-005527.
Cleared viewer cache on the server; revision showed after refresh.

evidence.text: Every listed ticket was resolved the same way, by clearing the viewer cache on the server, after which the new revision appeared.

quotes.quote: Cleared viewer cache on the server; revision showed after refresh.
Cleared viewer cache on the server; revision showed after refresh.

evidence.text: Users report the stale view on the same day as the release, which points to the release step rather than a slow nightly process.

quotes.quote: ECO released this morning but the viewer still shows revision B of 100-004520.
ECO released this morning but the viewer still shows revision B of 210-004240.

evidence.text: The problem hits many part-number families, not one part or product line, which suggests a systemic release-to-viewer gap.

quotes.quote: viewer still shows revision B of 450-005832

evidence.text: Plant users act on the drawings shown in the viewer, so a stale cache exposes them to superseded drawings after release.

quotes.quote: Plant sees the old drawing in the viewer after release.
Plant sees the old drawing in the viewer after release.

output.fix: Add an automated step to the ECO release workflow that invalidates or regenerates the viewer cache entries for every released item, so the viewer serves the new revision without manual cache clearing.
